notes: This was the last open structural question before the freeze, and it is now closed: ForVariableDeclaration is reachable and the SysML grammar has no unreachable production left.
decision: Adjudicated. SysML 8.2.2.17.7 states `ownedRelatedElement += UsageDeclaration`, and the rule departs from that literal text; the reasoning is recorded as the deviation ForVariableDeclarationMember, follow_xtext. UsageDeclaration is not an element — the pilot declares it a fragment (SysML.xtext:596), which contributes features to its caller's object rather than instantiating one — so it cannot be the target of a list-valued element assignment. The specification's own text settles which wrapper was meant: the three siblings in this clause each assign an element-producing production, 8.2.2.6.2 states the identical shape in `OwnedCrossFeatureMember` over `OwnedCrossFeature : ReferenceUsage = BasicUsagePrefix UsageDeclaration`, and `ownedRelatedElement += UsageDeclaration` appears in exactly one clause of the whole export, this one. Both readings accept the same text, so this changes no acceptance; it makes the clause's own ForVariableDeclaration reachable instead of orphaned.

evidence.note: States the production, and defines ForVariableDeclaration two lines below it.
The precedent: OwnedCrossFeatureMember assigns OwnedCrossFeature, a ReferenceUsage wrapper of UsageDeclaration, not UsageDeclaration itself.
Why the rule reads ForVariableDeclaration rather than UsageDeclaration.
Line 32 `for n : ScalarValues::Integer in (1, 2, 3) {` is the sole instance and does not separate the two readings; both consume it identically.
Second opinion, and the reading taken: it routes through ForVariableDeclaration (1637).
